newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil off highs on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil off highs on Iraq news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil came off the day's highs on news that Iraq was to deliver the annexes to its aid distribution plan on Monday.
A spokesman for the Iraqi mission to the United Nations in New York said on Monday that Iraq will deliver the annexes to the U.N. today.
September Brent moved off the intraday high of $18.70 to trade up just nine cents at $18.62 by 1435 GMT.
"The news from Iraq is the reason we're seeing a lid on the market," one broker said.
The prompt Brent contract had earlier moved to the highs of the day on the back of a stronger NYMEX opening but volume trade was relatively thin, brokers said.
On the September contract next resistance was at the July 17 high of $18.79 a barrel, with support around $18.45.
"The volume is pathetic and you could see a sharp move in this sort of scenario," another broker commented.
Gas oil was moving in line with Brent and the prompt August contract last moved unchanged on the day at $167.50 a tonne.
Good fund and trade buying on NYMEX gasoline and heating oil contracts supported prices on the NYMEX opening but these gains were quickly wiped away on the Iraqi news.

A senior U.N. official said on Monday that the U.N. Security Council late last week ruled out moving back the start date for Iraqi oil sales under the second round of their "oil-for-food" deal from June 8.

Iraq submitted its aid distribution plan to the U.N. secretary general last week and was asked to submit some additional documentation. Approval will allow oil exports under the second oil-for-food deal to resume.
